meta.title: Open BIM Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open BIM Studio: open source BIM modeller in development, built in DynLex. Direct modelling with Push/Pull, building systems, reinforcement, connections and drawings from the model, with IFCX as the project format.

header.label: Development preview · BIM modeller
header.title: Open BIM Studio
header.tagline: From sketch to reinforcement in one model
header.desc: A BIM modeller with a deliberately broad scope. On one side as direct as sketching: push, pull, try something and throw it away again. On the other side properly technical: building systems, reinforcement, connections and drawings from the same model. All on IFCX.

alt.hero: The example building in 3D: two storeys of layered walls with windows on piles, with the grid and a small plan
alt.pavilion: The foundation plan of an example pavilion with pad footings and ground beams with reinforcement, next to the reinforcement in 3D, a section and the reinforcement properties
alt.steel: A steel hall in 3D with columns, rafters, purlins and bracing
alt.plan: Structural plan of the example building with grids and hatched layered walls
alt.rebar: A plan with cages, wall and floor reinforcement and position labels
alt.schedule: A quantity schedule with walls, windows, doors, floors, piles and spaces
alt.elevation: The north elevation of the example building with storey levels and grid heads

notice.text: Not production-ready yet: this tool is in development. You can try it out, but do not use it for real project work yet. Report what you run into on GitHub.

features.label: Features
features.heading: One model, all outputs
features.sub: These are areas that have been built, not a promise that every combination is finished and tested.

direct.title: As direct as sketching
direct.desc: Draw a wall, drag a grip, push and pull a face. Levels, grids, layered walls, floors, roofs, columns, beams, piles and spaces live in the same model, and building systems, windows and stairs keep their parameters.

rebar.title: Reinforcement in the same model
rebar.desc: Parametric bars, cages, stirrups, area reinforcement and meshes, with position labels, bending schedules and Dutch or international notation. In 3D the reinforcement shows as lines so the model stays fast; one click shows the diameters.

steel.title: Connections you can still change later
steel.desc: End plates, fin plates, cleats, splices, gussets and base plates as parametric connections, with plates, bolts and welds. Save a connection as a type and use it again.

drawings.title: Drawings and schedules from the model
drawings.desc: Plans, sections, elevations, 3D views and quantity schedules come from the model instead of being drawn beside it. Put them on sheets and output them as PDF or SVG.

model.title: Building model
model.desc: Levels, grids, layered walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, openings, beams, columns, piles and spaces.

direct.title: Direct modelling
direct.desc: Selection, grips, numerical properties, snapping and transforms. Edit boundaries with Tab, Push/Pull and face splitting.

systems.title: Parametric systems
systems.desc: Building-system types with frames and panels, window systems hosted in the wall, stairs, railings and component libraries.

undo.title: Undo
undo.desc: Every change is a transaction in the model that you can undo and redo.

rebar.title: Reinforcement
rebar.desc: Parametric bars, cages, stirrups, area reinforcement and meshes.

rebarSchedule.title: Positions and bending schedules
rebarSchedule.desc: Position labels and schedules, in Dutch or international notation.

connections.title: Steel connections
connections.desc: Parametric joints, member cuts, plates, bolts and welds, with reusable connection types.

piles.title: Piles and foundations
piles.desc: Piles, pad footings and ground beams as ordinary elements in the model, with a pile plan of their own.

views.title: Plans, sections and elevations
views.desc: Derived from the model, with 3D views and section boxes.

annotate.title: Dimensions and tags
annotate.desc: Dimensions, tags and drawing standards that decide how each element is drawn.

sheets.title: Sheets as PDF or SVG
sheets.desc: Place views on a sheet and output it.

schedules.title: Quantity schedules
schedules.desc: Counts, lengths, areas and volumes per element type, exportable as CSV.

ifcx.title: IFCX as the project format
ifcx.desc: Save as IFCX, in JSON or binary, the open format of the OpenAEC ecosystem.

ifc.title: IFC in and out
ifc.desc: Supported IFC elements become editable objects; the rest stays read-only.

dxf.title: DXF
dxf.desc: Load DXF as reference geometry and export the plan or the model.

automation.title: Local API and MCP
automation.desc: Scripts and AI assistants operate the editor; every change is a single undo step.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v0.1.1
download.lead: Free and without an account. A development preview for Linux (x86-64), with an example building to start with.
download.metaLinux: Installer (.run) for Linux x86-64, with X11 and Vulkan
download.metaWindows: Linux only. There is no tested Windows version yet.
download.metaMac: Linux only. There is no macOS version.
download.mobileNote: Open BIM Studio is a desktop app for Linux. Download it on your computer.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.1.1
whatsnew.title: Reinforcement, section boxes and sketch editing
whatsnew.desc: The Linux preview of 23 October 2026 bundles the work that followed the first preview. It does not include a Windows installer yet.

rebar.title: Reinforcement
rebar.desc: Cages, bars, meshes and area reinforcement, with schedules and example models. Shown as light lines in 3D by default.

sectionbox.title: Section box and display
sectionbox.desc: Look inside the model with a section box and set the display and properties per view.

sketch.title: Sketch editing
sketch.desc: Develop free forms further in the model's sketch mode.

signed.title: IFC, DXF and a signed installer
signed.desc: Improvements in IFC and DXF exchange. The installer is signed with the OpenAEC OpenPGP key and listed in SHA256SUMS.

status.q: Can I use Open BIM Studio yet?
status.a: You can try the preview for Linux. It is a development version: file formats can still change and not every combination of features is finished or tested. Work with copies and do not use it for real projects yet.

cost.a: Nothing. The source code is licensed under MPL-2.0. You do not need an account and pay no licence fees.

platforms.q: Which systems does it run on?
platforms.a: For now only on Linux (x86-64) with glibc 2.38 or newer, an X11 session (or XWayland) and Vulkan. The Windows version is in the repository, but there is no tested installer yet. There is no macOS version.

try.q: How do I try it quickly?
try.a: Install the preview with bash Open-BIM-Studio-0.1.1-linux-x86_64.run and start it with ~/.local/bin/open-bim-studio --example. An example building opens: two storeys on piles, with grids, walls, windows and doors.

formats.q: Which files can I open and save?
formats.a: The project format is IFCX, as JSON or binary. IFC goes in and out, and drawings go to PDF or SVG. Supported IFC elements become editable objects; the rest stays read-only. So keep your source files.

dynlex.a: DynLex is the programming language we develop ourselves. The code reads almost like English sentences and compiles through LLVM to native code, so the modeller talks to the processor and the graphics card directly.

mcp.q: Can scripts or AI assistants operate the modeller?
mcp.a: Yes. The editor has a local API with an MCP adapter. An assistant can read the model, create walls, floors and grids, change properties and take screenshots. Every change is a single undo step, and everything runs only on your own computer.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: A native desktop app with its own CAD kernel, written entirely in DynLex.

dynlex.title: DynLex and LLVM
dynlex.desc: A small programming language that compiles to native code, with no runtime in between. DynLex on GitHub

kernel.title: Its own CAD kernel
kernel.desc: Planar, NURBS and B-rep geometry, from which the 2D and 3D views are derived.

model.title: Semantic BIM model
model.desc: Objects with their meaning, transactions and undo.

vulkan.title: Vulkan and GLFW
vulkan.desc: A native interface that drives the graphics card directly.

ifcx.title: IFCX and IFC
ifcx.desc: The open data format of the OpenAEC ecosystem, with IFC for exchange with other software.

mcp.title: Local API and MCP
mcp.desc: An automation interface that runs only on your own computer.
